about: Emergency numbers and free child/youth helplines that Hoot names when a child mentions self-harm or abuse. Keys are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. In each country the helplines are listed in order of preference; Hoot names the first one whose `topics` match what the child said ('self_harm' or 'abuse'), else the first one. Numbers were checked against the source URL shown (the helpline's own site or a government site). A child-safeguarding reviewer must re-check every entry, ideally by calling it, before launch and at least every 6 months. If a number cannot be confirmed, delete it: Hoot then falls back to its generic wording.
method: Checked on 2026-11-05 with web searches restricted to the official domain of each source URL (the build environment could not open pages directly), cross-checked against Child Helpline International's member directory where it lists the service.

emergency.notes: Emergency Response Support System (ERSS): police, fire and ambulance. Call, SMS or the 112 India app.

helplines.name: Child Helpline 1098
helplines.organisation: Ministry of Women and Child Development (Mission Vatsalya), integrated with ERSS-112
helplines.ages: children in distress, or an adult calling for them

helplines.name: Tele-MANAS
helplines.organisation: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (National Tele Mental Health Programme)

emergency.notes: Police, fire and ambulance. Text-to-911 only works in some areas.

helplines.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
helplines.organisation: 988 Lifeline (US Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration)
helplines.ages: all ages; you don't have to be suicidal to contact them

helplines.name: Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline
helplines.ages: children and adults worried about abuse; not a reporting line

emergency.notes: 112 also works. Police, fire, ambulance and coastguard. Deaf people can register for emergency SMS by texting 'register' to 999.

helplines.name: Childline
helplines.ages: children and young people; also in Welsh, and BSL via an interpreter

emergency.notes: Police, fire and ambulance. Some remote areas use local numbers.

helplines.name: Kids Help Phone
helplines.ages: young people; English and French, interpreters for other languages

emergency.notes: Triple Zero. 112 also works from mobile phones. You cannot text 000.
Gardaí, ambulance, fire and coastguard. 112 SMS is available for deaf and speech-impaired people.

helplines.name: Childline
helplines.note: Two childline.ie pages also offer text to 50101; most pages list only phone and chat, so text is left out until a reviewer confirms it.

emergency.notes: Police, fire and ambulance. Free, works on a mobile with no credit.

helplines.name: Youthline
helplines.ages: young people, or anyone supporting one
helplines.note: Older Youthline pages give text hours of 8am to midnight; the current helpline page says 24/7.

emergency.notes: 999 police; 995 SCDF fire and emergency ambulance. SMS 70995 for deaf, hard-of-hearing or speech-impaired people.

helplines.name: National Mindline 1771
helplines.note: Not toll-free (normal call charges). Chosen first because it is open 24/7; reviewers may prefer Tinkle Friend for primary-school children.

helplines.name: Tinkle Friend
helplines.hours: phone Mon–Fri 2.30–5pm; chat Mon–Thu 2.30–7pm, Fri 2.30–5pm; closed weekends and public holidays

emergency.notes: Ambulance: 10177. Local emergency numbers vary by municipality.

helplines.name: Childline South Africa
helplines.ages: children up to 18, and adults worried about a child
helplines.note: Online chat exists but only on weekdays (11am–1pm, 2pm–6pm), so it is not offered here.

emergency.notes: Unified national emergency hotline: police, fire and medical. Toll-free.

helplines.name: MAKABATA Helpline 1383
helplines.organisation: Council for the Welfare of Children (with DSWD)
helplines.ages: children, or anyone reporting abuse, neglect, bullying or mental-health concerns
helplines.note: Whether calls are free was not confirmed. Mobile numbers (Smart/Globe) are listed differently across sources, so they are left out.

helplines.name: NCMH Crisis Hotline
helplines.organisation: National Center for Mental Health (Department of Health)
helplines.note: Toll-free from landlines; some DOH pages say Luzon-wide only. NCMH also lists mobile numbers, which differ by a digit between sources, so they are left out.

emergency.notes: Toll-free from any network. Emergency centres are still being set up in some states.

helplines.name: Cece Yara Child Helpline
helplines.ages: children (adults can call to report or prevent abuse)
helplines.note: Focus is child sexual abuse; emergency response only in Lagos and Abuja, referrals elsewhere.

emergency.notes: National emergency numbers, answered by the Kenya Police.

helplines.name: Child Helpline 116
helplines.organisation: Department of Children Services with Childline Kenya
helplines.ages: children, and adults reporting violence against children
helplines.note: Childline Kenya also lists WhatsApp and SMS numbers, but they differ between pages, so they are left out.

helplines.name: Nummer gegen Kummer (Kinder- und Jugendtelefon)
helplines.hours: phone Mon–Sat 2–8pm; online counselling by email and chat (check the website for chat times)
helplines.note: Not 24/7. Reviewers may want to add a 24/7 crisis line for older teens.

emergency.notes: European emergency number, best from a mobile. Also 15 (SAMU, medical), 17 (police), 18 (fire), 114 (text/chat for deaf and hard-of-hearing people).

helplines.name: 119 – Allô Enfance en Danger
helplines.organisation: Service national d'accueil téléphonique de l'enfance en danger (SNATED)
helplines.ages: children and young people, or adults worried about a child; calls from children are prioritised

helplines.name: 3114 – Numéro national de prévention du suicide

emergency.notes: Free from any phone, even without a SIM card.

helplines.name: Teléfono ANAR de Ayuda a Niños y Adolescentes
helplines.note: ANAR also answers 116 111 in some regions (e.g. Comunitat Valenciana); 900 20 20 10 works nationwide.

emergency.notes: 112 reaches emergency services across the EU. Hoot keeps its generic wording for countries not listed above.

helplines.name: Child Helpline International: find a child helpline
helplines.hours: directory of member helplines by country
helplines.note: A directory, not a helpline. Shown to parents, not used in Hoot's replies.

droppedAsUnverified.name: Bantay Bata 163 (ABS-CBN Foundation)
droppedAsUnverified.reason: Became an online-only service on 1 April 2024; its current phone and chat channels could not be confirmed on an official page.

droppedAsUnverified.name: ISPCC Childline text 50101
droppedAsUnverified.reason: Listed on only two childline.ie pages; most pages list only phone and chat.
